title: BloombergGPT: A Large Language Model for Finance

task.value: Build a large language model specialized for financial NLP tasks (sentiment, NER, QA, etc.) while maintaining general-purpose LLM performance.
task.quote: For that reason, we set out to build a model that achieves best-in-class results on financial benchmarks, while also maintaining competitive performance on general-purpose LLM benchmarks.

architecture.value: Decoder-only causal LM based on BLOOM: 70 transformer layers, 40 heads, hidden dim 7,680, ALiBi positional encoding, extra embedding LayerNorm, Unigram tokenizer with 131,072 vocab; 50.6B parameters trained on 569B tokens.
architecture.quote: Our model is a decoder-only causal language model based on BLOOM (Scao et al., 2022). We present an overview of the architecture, with full details in Appendix A.

data.value: FinPile: 363B tokens of English financial web, news, filings, press releases and Bloomberg documents (2007-03-01 to 2022-07-31), plus 345B tokens of public data (The Pile, C4, Wikipedia).
data.quote: We construct a 363 billion token dataset based on Bloomberg’s extensive data sources, perhaps the largest domain-specific dataset yet, augmented with 345 billion tokens from general purpose datasets.

window.value: Training data ranged 2007 to June 2022; validation set contained only July 2022 data (~105M tokens); heldout loss test set is temporally after training.
window.quote: Our validation set only contained data from July 2022 (val {}_{\text{future}} ; roughly 105M tokens), whereas the training set ranged from 2007 to June 2022, meaning that the validation set was slightly out of distribution.

models.value: BloombergGPT, a 50 billion parameter BLOOM-style model trained from scratch; final checkpoint at step 139,200.
models.quote: We selected the checkpoint at step 139,200 as the final model based on validation loss and downstream evaluations.

baselines.value: GPT-NeoX, OPT 66B, BLOOM 176B (run by authors), plus reported GPT-3 and PaLM 540B numbers where available.
baselines.quote: We compare BloombergGPT to the three closest models described in § 7 based on model size, type of training data, overall performance, and most importantly, access.

headline_result.value: On public financial tasks, BloombergGPT averages 62.51 (win rate 0.93) vs GPT-NeoX 51.90, OPT66B 53.01, BLOOM176B 54.35.

costs.value: Training compute budget of 1.3M GPU hours on 40GB A100s; trained on 64x8 A100 40GB, ~53 days, 2.36e23 total FLOPs. No trading costs.
costs.quote: We start with a total compute budget of 1.3M GPU hours on 40GB A100 GPUs.

leakage_controls.value: Heldout test set is temporally after training and deduplicated against training; validation set from the future month; authors note internal unlabeled data likely appears in FinPile.
leakage_controls.quote: To limit data leakage and better simulate real-world usage of LLMs, we select a temporally heldout dataset that is strictly further in the future than the training set, and perform deduplication between the training and heldout set.

limitations.value: Internal evaluation data likely seen in pretraining; NER results mixed; claims restricted to LLM comparisons; training stopped early; cannot determine which changes stabilized training; toxicity/bias effects unknown.
limitations.quote: Note that, similar to the external datasets, it is likely that the unlabeled versions of the data used in our internal datasets occur in FinPile and are therefore seen by BloombergGPT during training.

release.value: Model and FinPile are not released; only Training Chronicles (Appendix C) are released.
release.quote: For this reason, we err on the side of caution and follow the practice of other LLM developers in not releasing our model.
